title: Assembly of a stabilizing sequence of cone approximations
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, C a cochain complex of R-modules in a fixed universe v, and b an integer. Let P_k be cochain complexes indexed by k in the natural numbers, f_k:P_k to C and j_k:P_k to P_(k+1) chain maps such that j_k followed by f_(k+1) equals f_k. Assume j_k is invertible in degree i whenever b+1-k≤i, and H^i(Cone(f_k))=0 whenever b+1-k≤i, where cohomology is computed in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then there is a constructed cochain complex F, a chain-level quasi-isomorphism g:F to C, and for every degree i a natural k and an isomorphism F^i with P_k^i. No finiteness or support assumption on P_k is made.

source.place: Tag 064U, proof of (2) implies (1), assembly of descending approximations; Lean realization by degreewise colimits; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064U

proof.text: Use Functor.ofSequence on j to make the diagram D. Apply the explicit Mathlib construction HomologicalComplex.coconeOfHasColimitEval D: its degree-i term is the module colimit, and its differential is induced from the stage differentials. The compatible f_k form a cocone, and the colimit universal property supplies g with each stage inclusion followed by g equal to f_k.

Fix i and k with b+1-k≤i. Every degree-i transition after k is invertible. Induct on the later index to show all transition composites from k are invertible. The degree-i diagram is therefore eventually constant from k. Apply Mathlib Functor.IsEventuallyConstantFrom.isIso_ι_of_isColimit to show its canonical inclusion from P_k^i is invertible. These are exactly the components of the stage chain maps into the degreewise colimit complex.

For degree i take k=(b+2-i).toNat. The stage inclusion is invertible in degrees i-1,i,i+1, so ShortComplex.quasiIso_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono proves it is a quasi-isomorphism in degree i. The cone vanishes in degrees i-1 and i, so [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] makes the map H^i(f_k) mono and epi, hence invertible. Transfer this through homologyFunctorFactors to chain cohomology and cancel the stage inclusion from f_k=inclusion followed by g, proving g is a quasi-isomorphism in degree i. For the requested term isomorphism take k=(b+1-i).toNat and invert the colimit inclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_model_of_stabilizing_cone_tower (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (b : ℤ)
    (P : ℕ → CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ)
    (f : ∀ k : ℕ, P k ⟶ C) (j : ∀ k : ℕ, P k ⟶ P (k + 1))
    (hcomm : ∀ k : ℕ, j k ≫ f (k + 1) = f k)
    (hstable : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : ℤ), b + 1 - (k : ℤ) ≤ i → IsIso ((j k).f i))
    (hvan : ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : ℤ), b + 1 - (k : ℤ) ≤ i → IsZero
      ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj (Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone (f k))))) :
    ∃ (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (g : F ⟶ C), QuasiIso g ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ k : ℕ, Nonempty (F.X i ≅ (P k).X i)
